text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Slovenian newspapers:
- Slovenian petrol prices have risen by 2.2 tolars (20 cents) per litre because of the imposition of a new ecological tax on January 1.
- Slovenian Primoz Peterka won the first ski-jumping competition this year, widening his lead in the World Cup.
- Parliament is expected to take a vote on Thursday on whether acting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek should lead the country's new government.
- Some 61 km (38 miles) of new motorways were built in Slovenia in 1996.
- Customs duties on goods imported from the European Union (EU) were reduced as of January 1 to conform with the provisions of Slovenia's association agreement with the EU.
- Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko shut down automatically on Wednesday because of a damaged steam pipe. The damage has yet to be repaired, officials said.
- Slovenian tourist resort managers said they were satisfied with the number of visitors over the New Year period.
